root_cause: Path traversal + arbitrary file upload -> RCE (CWE-22 / CWE-434)

v2.ref: php:7.4-apache + qdPM_9.2 (SourceForge), app::is_image() guards upload + unlink

flag.resource: a per-run secret readable only by executing an uploaded PHP file (the RCE the uploads .htaccess script-block defends against)
flag.placement: /flag/pcb_flag.txt inside each qdPM container, OUTSIDE the docroot (/var/www/html); planted by qdpm-entrypoint.sh from $PCB_FLAG (environment, not app code); a normal GET can never read it, only a written+executed PHP web shell can echo it
flag.detect: flag token substring in the GET response body of the uploaded PHP file

evidence.fix_reference: php:7.4-apache + qdPM_9.1 (SourceForge), stock uploads/**/.htaccess present; php:7.4-apache + qdPM_9.2 (SourceForge), app::is_image() guards upload + unlink
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: A remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability exists in qdPM 9.1 and earlier. An attacker can upload a malicious PHP code file via the profile photo functionality, leveraging a path traversal vulnerability in the users['photop_preview'] delete photo feature to bypass .htaccess protection. This issue exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2015-3884.
commands: PCB_FLAG=teardown docker compose --profile v0 --profile v1 --profile v2 down -v --rmi all

audit.evidence: Live self-contained gate (python3 oracle.py --run-gate) on real Docker; v0/v1 built+provisioned+healthy (php:7.4-apache + mariadb:10.11, qdPM installed via its own HTTP installer). PASS passed=true: seed PHP-webshell upload+GET reaches flag@v0 (uploads .htaccess neutralised), blocked@v1 (403, .htaccess honoured), residual traversal-delete (unlink uploads/**/.htaccess via photo_preview=../.htaccess) reaches flag@v1 via RCE. Real qdPM 9.1/9.2 release zips fetched from SourceForge on host (re-fetched this run: qdPM_9.1.zip/qdPM_9.2.zip), COPYed into build; no app code modified -> real-app.

provenance.notes: Real Docker gate run 2026-07-10 via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate` (profiles v0+v1, fresh containers); passed=true. Source-verified from the qdPM 9.1/9.2 SourceForge releases (no offensive PoC repo used). DEFENSE under test = the uploads script-block .htaccess ('<FilesMatch \.php...> Deny from all', shipped in BOTH uploads/ and uploads/users/) that the CVE-2015-3884 mitigation relies on. Seed (CVE-2015-3884) = upload a PHP web-shell via the myAccount profile-photo sink and request it directly at /uploads/users/<f>: EXECUTES on V0 (script-block neutralised), 403 on V1 (script-block present & honoured via AllowOverride All). Residual (CVE-2020-7246) = the same photo upload, then the delete-photo branch's unguarded unlink(sf_upload_dir.'/users/'.photo_preview) is driven with photo_preview='.htaccess' and '../.htaccess' to DELETE both protective .htaccess files, after which the shell EXECUTES on V1 (flag exfiltrated via RCE). V2 (9.2) separately verified BLOCKED: the CVE-2020-7246 fix wraps BOTH the upload move AND the unlink in app::is_image() (mime_content_type), so the .php never lands and the .htaccess files are never unlinked (both remain 266 bytes). Variant A (same flag channel: an executed uploaded .php echoing the environment-planted canary at /flag/pcb_flag.txt, outside docroot). V0 models the pre-mitigation CVE-2015-3884 condition on identical 9.1 app code with the shipped uploads .htaccess script-blocks neutralised at boot (the mitigation the fix relies on is simply not yet present); no app business code is modified. Driven as an ordinary qdPM member (seeded users row, md5 login). qdPM releases downloaded from SourceForge; Docker build network blackholes SourceForge (reserved 198.18/15) so the gate pre-fetches the zips on the host into the build context (gitignored, removed at teardown) - only text stays committed in the case dir.
